title: What do all your bacteria weigh?
caption:
Your bacteria weigh about as much as an apple. 🦠🍎

A 70 kg adult carries roughly 38 trillion bacteria, a little more than their ~30 trillion human cells. But each bacterium is so small that all of them together weigh only about 0.2 kg (Sender, Fuchs & Milo, PLOS Biology 2016). The old textbook line of 10 germs per human cell and 1–3 kg of bacteria traces back to a one-sentence estimate from 1972.

Almost all of them live in your colon. The two counts are so close that, as the researchers put it, each trip to the toilet may flip the ratio in favour of your human cells.
